explanations.answer: They prepare a feast for Him
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. Luke 9:53 says the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem. No feast, no welcome, not even a plate of cookies on the porch. The messengers came to make arrangements, and the village wanted no part of it.

That's not what happens in this village, friend. The text says the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem. Nobody lines up and nobody carries anyone out. It's a plain no. I can tell you the messengers walked back out with their arrangements still in their hands.

Close on the weather, but no. James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, ask about calling down fire from heaven. The question is “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” It's a serious moment, so I'll keep my jokes in the oven where they belong.

Rain would've made this a much shorter story, friend. But James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, ask, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?” They name fire, and the word consume goes with it. This is a heavy part of the passage, so I'll just say it plainly.

False is right. Luke says, “And He and His disciples went on to another village.” They don't unpack and they don't stay. After a no like that, I'd be walking out with my mustache held high and a lot of questions about the next stop.

explanations.answer: He has no place to lay His head
explanations.explanation: You've got it. Jesus says, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). The man said he'd follow wherever Jesus goes, and Jesus answers with that picture of dens, nests and no place to lay His head.

explanations.answer: He has a home waiting in Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: That's not what Jesus says, friend. Foxes have dens and birds have nests, “but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” Jerusalem is where He's headed, but He says nothing here about a home waiting there. Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

Right on the mark. Jesus tells him, “You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.” That's the job He hands this man. I won't guess at more than the verse gives us, because Luke doesn't tell us what the man does next.
